description: Delaware-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Where no special hazard exists, Delaware's speed in a business district is
questions.explanation: 21 Del. C. section 4169(a)(1) makes 25 miles per hour lawful in any business district. A speed over the limits in subsection (a) is absolute evidence that the speed is not reasonable or prudent.

questions.q: In a Delaware residence district, the statutory speed is
options: 20 or 25 mph, per the road owner
15 mph when no sign is posted
questions.explanation: Section 4169(a)(2) says 20 or 25 miles per hour in any residence district, at the discretion of the agency owning the roadway.

questions.q: Delaware's 20 mph school-zone speed applies
options: At every school whether or not a sign is posted
Where posted 20 mph signs state when it applies
Only when a school bus is loading
On interstate highways through a city
questions.explanation: Section 4169(a)(3) sets 20 miles per hour at school zones where 20 mph regulatory signs are posted and state the time periods or conditions. Those conditions may include when children are present or while one or more warning lights flash.

questions.q: Delaware sets a 65 mph maximum on State Route 1
options: For the entire length of the route
From Red Lion Creek to Appoquinimink
questions.explanation: Section 4169(d) requires the Department of Transportation to designate 65 miles per hour for those portions of Delaware State Route 1, except the delineated nonhighway-speed toll-plaza area. The limit may be posted on fixed or variable signs.

questions.q: Delaware prohibits driving when the person's alcohol concentration is
options: .08 or more, up to 4 hours after
questions.explanation: 21 Del. C. section 4177(a) prohibits driving when the alcohol concentration is .08 or more, and also when it is .08 or more within 4 hours after driving if that concentration resulted from alcohol present in or consumed by the person while driving.

questions.q: A person under 21 violates Delaware's underage driving law by driving
options: Only if a chemical test is refused
questions.explanation: Section 4177L(a) applies to whoever, being under 21, drives, operates, or has actual physical control of a vehicle, off-highway vehicle, or moped while consuming or after having consumed alcoholic liquor.

questions.q: In a Delaware under-21 proceeding, an alcohol concentration of .02 or more within 4 hours is
options: Irrelevant if the person denies drinking
Per se evidence that the person had consumed alcoholic liquor
Proof of adult DUI by itself
Required before any under-21 charge can be filed
questions.explanation: Section 4177L(b) says evidence of an alcohol concentration of .02 or more in the blood or breath is per se evidence that the underage person had consumed alcoholic liquor. The same subsection says a conviction may still be based on other admissible evidence.

questions.q: At 8 calculated points, Delaware DMV's problem-driver actions begin with
questions.explanation: The Delaware DMV point page says 8 calculated points produce an advisory letter. Calculated points count at full value for the first 12 months from the violation date and at half value for the next 12 months. Actions use the total within a 24-month period.

questions.q: At 12 calculated points, Delaware requires the driver to
questions.explanation: The DMV page says that at 12 calculated points the driver must complete that course within 90 days after notification, unless DMV extends the time. Failure to comply, or the driver's preference, results in a mandatory 2-month suspension.

questions.q: A Delaware Level One Learner's Permit is for an applicant who is
questions.explanation: The Delaware DMV Level One page states those age rules and requires a Delaware Driver Education Certificate, or Department of Education approval of an out-of-state course. At least 16 and less than 18, or on an active IEP and at least 16 and less than 22.

questions.q: For the first six months of a Delaware Level One Learner's Permit, the holder must
questions.explanation: The DMV page says supervision is required at all times during the first six months, and the sponsor certifies 50 hours including 10 hours of nighttime driving. That certification is turned in to the Department of Education after the first six months.

questions.q: During the first 12 months of a Delaware Level One permit, passengers are limited to
options: The supervisor and one other rider
questions.explanation: The DMV page says no passengers other than the adult supervisor and one other passenger during the entire first 12 months, except immediate family members when the adult supervisor is in the car. During the second six months of unsupervised driving, when a supervisor is not present, only one other passenger besides the driver is allowed. The permit holder also shall not use a cellular telephone, text-messaging device, or similar electronic device.

questions.q: In Delaware, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Delaware requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Delaware complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Delaware requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Delaware teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Delaware requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Delaware: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Drivers License/Identification Cards - Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Delaware, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Delaware, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16½ years.

provenance.manual: Drivers License/Identification Cards - Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Delaware, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Delaware drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Delaware car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Delaware car knowledge test has 32 questions.

provenance.manual: Drivers License/Identification Cards - Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Delaware car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Delaware car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Delaware, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Delaware, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Delaware, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Delaware, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Delaware sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Delaware, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Delaware brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Delaware, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Delaware?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Delaware can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Delaware rural interstate: up to 65 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Delaware's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Delaware: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Delaware?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Delaware, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Delaware left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Delaware's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Delaware seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: What is Delaware's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Delaware requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $10,000.

questions.q: Under Delaware's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Delaware can suspend an adult's license at 14 points in 24 months.
